A few expeditions were completely anihilated by the natives. And why did they started the expeditions? Well, they heard about gold and silver in the Incan Empire… Do the math… After some expeditions had become succesful, Sao Paulo grew in importance, again for trade. But what made Sao Paulo really rich was to find out that the soil and climate were perfect for coffee crops, after that Sao Paulo only became more developed and rich, until it became the Brazil’s leading city. It was never planned by the rulers because it wasn’t near a huge river, nor the shore, it just happened. I think Sao Paulo was a hub before colonization because it’s really close to the sea but the steep barrier of range of mountains made it difficult the last passage to the shore. But Sao Paulo is, at same time, easy to reach it through many rivers. Looks like the natives would reach that area, trade between them and then go back to their lands, some of them, across the mountains. The Peabiru trail could connect both the Atlantic and Pacific ocean, before the arrival of the Portugueses. Sao Paulo’s downtown is full of indigenous trails, names and history. For the common people the fall of the Empire took a long time to be noticed and their lives actually improved in many aspects. They weren’t slaves anymore, but serves. They could take most of their own lives decisions. They could have their diseases treated by the churches, monasteries. They had holidays, could get married and had land (of their lord) to work on it, not begging for food like during the Roman times. Now comparing to USA, if US fall suddenly by being attacked, there would be a deep degradation. Especially in the Western world. Many knowledge would be lost, not the knowledge itself, but people that are able to put that knowledge into the real world. The know-how. We, as society would have more urgent priorities, such as reconstruction and saving lives. The fine of technology would be taken care from distant parts of the world, not affected by the war. If it would be a slow fall, no one would notice or care. Because everything would be slowly absorbed and developed out of USA, just like the city of Rome was declining. Question: Why are many African countries still underdeveloped, despite huge natural resources?

At that time they already couldn’t compete in trade with other countries. So people were exposed to new goods, new technologies, new weapons, they wanted those things for them too. It doesn’t help when colonialists appear and make your territory just a place to extract resources, even bringing railroads, bridges, vaccines, it doesn’t change the social reality. If Africa still keep their endless ethnic conflicts they won’t strive. If they still keep dictators controlling everything, they will stay behind. Just like Latin America, from where I am. Good institutions make a developed country, not resources. There is even a good book detailing that: Why Nations Fail. I strongly recommend reading it.

Question: What's the worst that could happen if you go into business with a close friend or family member?

Everything done, time to open! December, 10th. It was being a good month, unfortunately, very short, because as soon as Christmas approach, people aren’t consuming anymore, it’s just holidays now and in Brazil is Summer. So people start to travel. Not consuming at all. Anyway January is a good month, good sales. Which is a surprise, because people are traveling, going to the beaches. Then comes February, the carnival month. Brazil doesn’t work in February, everything is postponed for post-Carnival. Anyway, profit. March is the month she will arrive in Brazil, but a change happened. She didn’t want to come any longer. She was fine where she was. At the time she comes, sales plummeted a bit, because we had a lockdown due to Covid-19 (who could have ever expect that???). She just came but she is never happy. The days are boring, slow business, nothing else to do because, except for a few exceptions (like our business) everything is closed. Second month like that, April. Everything is slow and nothing to do. She’s very stressed, me too. But I have to work, because I’m the only one now that knows how to run the business and she is not really willing to learn, except when she is in good mood. I don’t have that luxury to avoid going to work, but I’m fine. Long story short, now she hates me, she wants to leave, sell her half of the business and depart (she is not Brazilian). Lesson learned: The most important thing about a business, more important than find a good field to operate, good location, strategy, plans, etc. It’s having a good partner, all the other things can be easily solved with a good partner. That’s my story and is happening right now.

Question: Why is Dubai called a fake city?

The shining buildings tend to disappear there. When you are at the “main” places, the only people you see in public parks or public spaces, trees and grass are the menial workers. They can’t afford to be visiting all the shinning places. There is a invisible, non written, accepted behavior to follow. I remember when once living in a very, very suburban area in Abu Dhabi, police had stopped me and my friends because we were jogging at 10pm, like “what do you think you doing?”. It was a quiet place, you couldn’t see anyone doing normal things at their own streets. There is no life on the streets. That’s one of the reasons behind the “Fake city vibe”. I’m not saying you can’t jog around, because you can, but there will be places that just feel weird. Nightlife is interesting. You can find Arab (Levant) clubs, Filipino clubs, African, Indian clubs and International clubs. By international I mean “for white people”. It doesn’t mean exclusively for white people, but they are aiming for white people or general high income people. And people will be dressed the same, listening to the same music everywhere. The owners can’t even take the risk to play something different. Homogenous is the rule. Oh, I almost forgot, people go searching places that looks “classy”, but most people there aren’t classy, they are trying to look like that. One night stands can happen all the time. But clubs are full of prostitutes disguised as regular guests. Half of the Tinder is composed of prostitutes too. Beautiful women know they are in high demand. So they are even more demanding, be prepared to find gold diggers everywhere. Dating scene kind of suck. Dubai it’s a city made to make you spend, to make you consume. Do you wanna go to the beach? There is the public beach, but you can’t drink alcohol. Do you wanna drink alcohol? Go to the clubs and get overpriced drinks. If you have a family, girlfriend/boyfriend, life can be easier, but there is always the feeling that you have no one else to talk. It’s strange because everyone complain about that, but no one is willing to change their own behavior. In Dubai there is not that easy going vibe you can find in other cities, like you you just go to pub or bar near your home, just to have a beer and relax, talk to some random people. If you have bars near your home that people are not dressed to impress, so it’s not a good bar. You prefer not going there. When you live in a big international city, you have many options of things to do. In Dubai the main entertainment is: Going to the Mall, buy some stuff and have a dinner inside some big chain restaurant. Cool, isn’t? Movies? Mostly Blockbusters. Another thing? Ok, some water parks. Although I admit I used to love Ski Dubai. I learned snowboarding there. They have dinner in the sky, sky diving, jet ski etc. They are nice, but they aren’t things you do when you have a regular life. Those are things for tourists. Even nature (the best places) are controlled. Many “don’ts” Everything there is for taking pictures, not to feel that they are there for you. Having new friends is hard. It’s almost like they are saying: you are here to make money and leave. Or else, spend here all the money you got here. I left Dubai during the pandemic, company not paying salaries, bills are high, I left. I could go back someday, but I know how it is. You know one of the favorite things people do in Dubai? Travel to another place Just a curiosity: I remember when I was checking my drone during the night in a parking lot. Later on, checking the videos I saw many truck drivers sleeping in their trucks, most of them Pakistanis. They didn’t have money to pay an accommodation. Adding a few more notes: Dubai doesn’t have an identity. Many people here can say “They are Muslim”, but can you imagine going to the Netherlands, coming back and saying “They are Christians”? That’s the kind of opinion that shows exactly why Dubai is fake. You can’t compare the beautiful parks and gardens like, for example, Vienna. They have astounding gardens, in the middle of the city, they are part of the landscape, not something you have to drive for 20 minutes and pay to see. And a very tacky design… You want nice beaches? Mediterranean, Caribbean, Asia, Miami are better. Amusement Parks? Orlando, Florida, they offer more value to your investment. Shopping? USA too. Arab World? Middle East offers a better experience. It’s not as sterilized as Dubai, you have to “dirt your feet” but it’s more authentic. Dubai have this: Stunning views. Question: What was your scariest travel experience?
Answer: Gypsies I was in Romania, going from Brasov to Sighisoara, it was already dusk. I got on the train and the train was old. There are several types of trains in Romania, from good to bad, but this was particularly bad. Old, poorly maintained, dirty and to make matters worse, it had those enclosed compartments that people in groups use to occupy some seats and say that all of them are occupied. I was going through the train trying to find some available seat and being optimistic I decided to ask about a seat in a compartment with the elderly inside. Excuse me, I sat down, I packed my bag and tried to rest. But I felt tense inside. They seemed to be very simple people, old clothes, worn out. They smelled bad, they smelled of urine, cigarettes, dirt, they looked like homeless people. I decided to leave the compartment and stay near the toilet area of the train. Using a wooden stool that it was beside it. After a few minutes there, a guy comes and asks if I have a cigarette, "I don't smoke," I told him. He finds a cigarette and starts smoking next to the open train door. He starts to look me up and down, and then he starts asking questions with a very bad English. "Where are you from? What are you doing here? How long are you staying? What do you want to do here?" this kind of thing. Normal questions, but not in the best circumstance. I always travel with little luggage and I believe that my relatively small and ordinary backpack is not appealing to criminals. But I had two cellphones, a drone and an action camera inside, plus the money in my wallet and credit cards. I was tense to lose everything. In Brazil, a type of situation like this you run the risk of having a gun pointed at your head, I know that in Romania this type of situation is rare, but I was inside a train that did not seem to be the most frequented and was full of gypsies. And gypsies do not have the best of fame. Between the "difficult" decision to worry about my security or worry about the politically correct, I choose the first alternative. He ended up leaving and I felt relieved for a moment, but knowing that I was in a moving place (near the bathroom) I felt I should keep a few things in safer places. A few minutes went by and now the whole group of gypsies, including the previous guy, come. It all happens again, they keep looking at me, they wave. They ask for a cigarette, they ask for a cigarette lighter and I say again that I do not smoke. I was drinking a beer and I was afraid that would give them more freedom to try to get close to me. One of them spoke a better English and started asking questions, when I said that I was Brazilian (which I consider an international green card in relation to being well received by people in general, you know, football, samba, carnival), then the questions started to become more normal, like football, beaches, parties, women, etc. Even so I still felt tense. If they wanted to rob me, they could easily now, as they were in 5 or 6 people. After a few minutes of conversation I realized that their station was approaching. They start offering me products (where did they take them from?), Drugs, and even women. Where I later heard it is a very common gypsy trick. They offer a prostitute and when the customer goes to the room, he is robbed. In the end they did not do me any harm, they said goodbye and most of the passengers getting off the train and almost everyone seems to be gypsies. When you arrive in Romania you realize how easy it is to identify them. But before they left, they saw me leaving the stool, so they came back and asked me to hand the stool over to them. He grabbed and said "Timber!". It was in November, cold in Romania. But now the train was almost empty, I was able to choose a seat to stay and rest well until arriving in Sighisoara. But it was a situation that left me worried, being stolen inside a moving train, losing money, documents and valuables and then arriving in an unknown city and at dawn ... Not a good perspective. I suspect that being a Brazilian (poor country, but hiding the fact that I live in Dubai), having a simple backpack and walking with torn jeans could have saved me from something worse. Fortunately nothing happened, I continued my trip through Romania and it is a wonderful country. I'll be back in January now, 2019. Question: What human in world history is the closest we had to a super hero in terms of strength, intelligence, unnatural abilities, etc.?
Answer: A man called “Modern Viking”, Gulli Fridporsson. The weather on the night of Sunday, March 11, 1984, wasn't especially bad. The air temperature was 28F (-2C) but that was normal for winter in the Westman Islands, an archipelago off the south coast of Iceland. But that didn't prevent catastrophe for the crew of the Hellisey VE-503, a fishing boat that had left harbour only a few hours earlier. A boat that capsized in the freezing water. The crew of five were pitched into the biting cold water. At 41F (5C) it was slightly warmer than the air but the human body loses heat 25 times faster in water so the men were in extreme peril. Two of them were trapped below deck and failed to make it to the surface. The other three clambered on to the upended keel. Determined not to die without a fight the three men began to swim. One of them soon lost consciousness and drowned. The other two, the captain Hjortur Jonsson and the young mate Gulli Fridporsson, swam side by side and tried to keep talking but after a few minutes Fridporsson was alone. He should have died too. In those conditions the longest someone can expect to survive is 30 minutes but that's not what happened to this lone swimmer dressed in just jeans, a shirt and a sweater and with nothing on his feet, having discarded his boots and oilskins. Talking to seagulls hovering above him to try and stay alert he passed within 300ft of a boat but no one heard his calls or saw him waving. After six hours in the sea he reached land. Fridporsson then faced a two-mile barefoot walk over rough lava slopes in soaking wet clothes. He finally knocked on a villager's door at seven o'clock the next morning leaving a trail of bloody footprints in the snow. This true story, well known in Iceland, has now been told for a wider audience in a film called The Deep. It’s not an exciting movie, but is real story. Researchers at the University of Iceland determined that the overweight Fridp³rsson's body fat was like that of a seal: it was more solid than normal human fat and two or three times thicker than the average of 7 to 9mm. Dubbed "The Human Seal" by the Icelandic media he was even more remarkable than British swimmer Lewis Pugh who was described as the human polar bear after swimming in just Speedo trunks and goggles in the Arctic and Antarctic. Pugh, who swims in the world's coldest regions to draw attention to the melting ice-caps is an athlete who has trained himself to raise his body temperature by concentrating on raising his heart rate. Fridporsson by contrast had no interest in sport. In the film, when asked what his game of choice is, he says he is pretty good at chess. Fridporsson, who had been asked to sit pedalling an exercise bicycle in a vat of iced water alongside strapping soldiers who gave up within minutes while he could go on and on without stopping, grew tired of being treated as a guinea pig. Plagued by survivor guilt and having no wish to capitalise on his superhuman feat he disliked his celebrity status and yearned to get back to his own community and simple way of life.He returned to the sea in 1987 and continued to work as a trawlerman for several years. Now 51 and married he works for a seafood company. He served on the island council until last September. In this answer I used parts of a report from Express UK. It’s a very interesting story that I could know because of the movie. The man could survive in extreme cold temperature naturally. No training, no exercises, nothing. It’s a natural gift. More details you can find here. The strange story of the human seal https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gu%C3%B0laugur_Fri%C3%B0%C3%BE%C3%B3rsson And the movie about him. The Deep – review
